rv.q: Despite a few transfixing moments, this misconceived hybrid of concert and theatrical spectacle feels overblown and undercooked.
The weakness of the venture is that it seems likely to make many theatregoers impatient to experience the novel or the Wayne recording instead.
The director, Bob Tomson, does his best to bring it to life, but struggles to create human drama in a script that’s better imagined than staged.
This is high-end cheese, and at points it's delightfully entertaining as such.
HG Wells must be rolling in his grave.
You can’t fault this on spectacle, and you can’t fault Wayne on his rockingly good creation.
But the brilliance of the presentation cannot conceal the thinness of the content.

cn.t: Jeff Wayne's prog-rock spectacle divides critics with its visual bombast and iconic score, but most find the theatrical adaptation overblown and undercooked, struggling to translate the beloved concept album into compelling drama.
